question.name: CSEC Phy May 2022 Q4a(i) — Define Pressure and State SI Unit
question.text:
Define the term 'pressure' by completing the statement, and state its SI unit.

Pressure is the [[1]] acting per unit [[2]].

The SI unit of pressure is the [[3]].
question.general_feedback:
Pressure definition:

Pressure is the force acting per unit area.

Formula: P = F / A

SI unit: Pascal (Pa) = N m⁻² (Newton per square metre)

Examples:

  • A sharp knife has a small area → large pressure per unit area → cuts easily
  • Snowshoes spread weight over large area → reduce pressure → prevent sinking in snow
  • Atmospheric pressure at sea level ≈ 101 325 Pa ≈ 1 × 10⁵ Pa

groups.label: Pressure = ___ per unit area
groups.diagnostic_hint: Pressure = FORCE per unit area (P = F/A). Force is applied perpendicular to the surface. Greater force or smaller area → greater pressure.

groups.label: Pressure = force per unit ___
groups.diagnostic_hint: Pressure = force per unit AREA. The area is the surface area over which the force is distributed. Smaller area = more concentrated force = higher pressure.

groups.label: SI unit of pressure
groups.diagnostic_hint: The SI unit of pressure is the PASCAL (Pa), equivalent to 1 N m⁻² (newton per square metre). Named after Blaise Pascal.

ddwtos.word_bank_note: 11 tokens for 3 slots. Slot 1 (force): 'mass' is wrong — mass is not a force. 'Weight' is a force (mg) but pressure is defined using generic 'force', not specifically weight. 'Energy' is wrong. Slot 2 (area): 'volume' is wrong — pressure is per unit AREA (2D), not volume (3D). That would be concentration or energy density. Slot 3 (pascal): the newton is the unit of FORCE (not pressure). The joule is the unit of energy. The watt is power.
